newsitem.title: USA: Two U.S. lawmakers seek insurance for birth control.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. lawmakers seek insurance for birth control.

text.p: A bipartisan pair of senators Wednesday proposed a bill to expand health insurance coverage of birth control, a measure they said could reduce the number of U.S. abortions.
Sen. Harry Reid, a Nevada Democrat, and Sen. Olympia Snowe, a Maine Republican, said expanding access to affordable contraceptives would reduce the number of unintended pregnancies.
The bill would require insurance plans that cover prescription drugs to include contraceptive drugs and devices. It would not apply to plans that do not cover drugs.
"A woman's insurance often covers a prescription to alleviate allergy symptoms but not a prescription to prevent an unintended and life-altering pregnancy," Snowe said.
The sponsors quoted a study by the Alan Guttmacher Institute that shows that half of insurance plans do not cover prescription contraceptives, although 90 percent cover prescription drugs.

The bill was one of several introduced in the past two years that attempted to regulate narrow aspects of insurance coverage. Several, including bills that specified minimum hospital stays for mastectomy and childbirth, dealt with women's health.

Planned Parenthood Federation hailed the Snowe-Reid proposal. "It would begin to close the unacceptable gender-based gap in insurance coverage that has long frustrated and baffled American women," the group said in a statement.
"Creating barriers to contraception increases the numbers of unintended pregnancies and abortions and threatens the physical and financial well-being of women and families," it added.
